masterIndex.approxDates2026: Every 11th tithi of each fortnight; next: Sep 7 (Aja Ekadashi)
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on the 11th lunar day dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Only specific foods allowed — no grains, no rice, no regular salt. One of the most widely observed Hindu fasts.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Women primarily; all devotees of Devi
masterIndex.briefDescription: Nine nights of fasting during Chaitra and Sharad Navratri. Special sattvic diet with kuttu flour, singhara flour, sabudana. No onion, garlic, non-veg.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: Every Monday; especially sacred during Shravan (Jul 30 – Aug 28)
masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Shiva devotees; unmarried girls; married women
masterIndex.briefDescription: Weekly fast on Monday devoted to Lord Shiva. One meal a day, vegetarian. Especially important during Shravan month.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Hanuman devotees; those with Mangal dosha
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on Tuesday for Lord Hanuman. One meal a day. Some traditions avoid wheat and salt.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Those seeking wisdom/prosperity; Sai Baba devotees
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on Thursday. Yellow-colored foods preferred (chana dal, banana, turmeric). One meal a day.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Women seeking wealth and harmony; Santoshi Maa devotees
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on Friday for Goddess Lakshmi or Santoshi Maa. Sweet foods, no sour items (citrus, tamarind, pickles).

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Those with Shani dosha; general devotees
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on Saturday to appease Lord Shani. Black-colored foods (black sesame, urad dal). One meal after sunset in some traditions.
Married women fast without food or water from sunrise until they sight the moon at night. Observed for the long life of husbands.
One of the hardest Hindu fasts — 36 hours without water. Devotees stand in water offering arghya to the Sun. Strict purity observed.
Fast on the 13th day of each lunar fortnight, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Puja performed during Pradosh Kaal (twilight period).
Monthly fast on the 4th day of Krishna Paksha for Lord Ganesha. Fast broken after sighting the moon.
Puja and light fast on full moon day. Katha (story) is read. Prasad made of suji, banana, ghee is distributed.
Night-long worship of Lord Shiva. Strict fast — some do nirjala (no water). Fast broken next morning.
Fast on Krishna's birthday. No grains until midnight. Fast broken after midnight puja. Some do nirjala.
Fast on Lord Rama's birthday. Fruits and milk allowed. Some observe it as part of Chaitra Navratri.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: All Hindus; especially Maharashtra, AP, Karnataka
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on the first day of Ganesh Chaturthi festival. Modak (sweet dumpling) is the traditional offering. Festival lasts 1 to 11 days.
Mothers fast for the well-being and long life of their children. Fast broken after sighting stars at night.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: Hariyali Teej: Aug 11; Hartalika Teej: Aug 26, 2026
masterIndex.briefDescription: Women's fast for marital bliss and good spouse. Hartalika Teej is nirjala (no water). Celebrated with henna, swings, and green bangles.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: Shiva devotees; unmarried girls; married women
masterIndex.briefDescription: Special Monday fasts during the holy month of Shravan. More meritorious than regular Monday fasts. Kanwariyas carry Ganga jal.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: Every full moon day (12 per year)
masterIndex.briefDescription: Light fast on full moon day. Sattvic food. Often combined with Satyanarayan Katha.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: Every new moon day (12 per year)
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fast on new moon day, often for remembering ancestors. Tarpan (water offering) performed.

masterIndex.whoTypicallyObserves: All Jains — the most important Jain festival
masterIndex.briefDescription: The holiest period in Jainism. Intensive fasting, meditation, study of Kalpa Sutra. Some do complete water-only fasts for 8 days. Ends with Michhami Dukkadam (universal forgiveness).
Each of the 10 days dedicated to one virtue (Forgiveness, Humility, Straightforwardness, Truth, Cleanliness, Self-restraint, Penance, Renunciation, Non-attachment, Celibacy). Fasting and meditation.
Nine days of Ayambil — eating only ONE plain meal per day. The meal contains only boiled grains/pulses, NO oil, NO spices, NO salt, NO sugar, NO ghee, NO milk. Very austere diet.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: Any day chosen by the practitioner
masterIndex.briefDescription: Eating only ONE meal in a single sitting per day. No snacking. Water allowed. A very common Jain daily practice, especially during festivals.

masterIndex.frequency: Any day (personal choice; common during festivals)
masterIndex.briefDescription: Complete abstention from food for 24 hours. Only boiled water allowed before sunset. No food from sunset to next day's sunset.
Eight consecutive days of complete fasting (no food, only water). One of the most rigorous fasts in any Indian religion.
Year-long alternate-day fasting — eat one day, fast completely the next, for over 13 months. Broken with sugarcane juice on Akshaya Tritiya. Extremely rare and revered.
ALWAYS avoid: all root vegetables (potato, onion, garlic, carrot, radish, ginger, beetroot, turnip — pulling them kills the plant), non-veg, eggs, honey. No eating after sunset. No fermented food.
Birthday of Lord Mahavir. Prayer, procession (rath yatra), and light fasting. Charity and compassion emphasized.

masterIndex.deityOrPurpose: One of the Five Pillars of Islam
masterIndex.approxDates2026: Feb 18 – Mar 19, 2026 (approx; depends on moon sighting)
masterIndex.briefDescription: Month-long dawn-to-sunset fast. No food, water, or smoking from Fajr (pre-dawn) to Maghrib (sunset). Suhoor = pre-dawn meal. Iftar = sunset meal. Exemptions for children, elderly, sick, pregnant, menstruating, travelers.
Fast on the 10th of Muharram (and preferably 9th also). Sunni tradition: Prophet Muhammad fasted this day. Shia Muslims observe Ashura as a day of mourning for Imam Hussain.
Six voluntary fasts during the month of Shawwal (after Eid ul-Fitr). A hadith says fasting Ramadan + 6 of Shawwal equals fasting the whole year.
Fast on the day before Eid ul-Adha. A hadith says it expiates sins of the previous and coming year. Pilgrims at Hajj do NOT fast this day.
Prophet Muhammad is reported to have regularly fasted on Mondays and Thursdays. Voluntary but considered highly meritorious.
Voluntary fasting in the month before Ramadan. Prophet Muhammad reportedly fasted most of Sha'ban. Includes Shab-e-Barat (15th Sha'ban) observances.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: 3 days around each full moon in the Islamic calendar
masterIndex.briefDescription: Fasting on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of each Islamic lunar month — the "bright/white" days when the moon is full. Voluntary but meritorious.

masterIndex.durationPerOccurrence: N/A — not a formal fast tradition
masterIndex.approxDates2026: N/A — Sikhism generally discourages ritualistic fasting
masterIndex.briefDescription: Sikh Gurus generally discouraged ritualistic fasting, seeing it as empty ritual. However: Amritdhari (baptised) Sikhs avoid halal meat, tobacco, and intoxicants permanently. Some Sikhs voluntarily eat simple vegetarian langar-style food on Gurpurabs. The focus is on Langar (communal meal) rather than fasting.

masterIndex.approxDates2026: Guru Nanak Gurpurab: Nov 5, 2026; Guru Gobind Singh: Jan 5, 2026; Vaisakhi: Apr 14, 2026
masterIndex.briefDescription: Gurpurabs celebrate Guru birthdays/martyrdoms with Akhand Path (48-hour scripture reading), Nagar Kirtan (procession), and Langar (free community meal). The emphasis is on communal eating, not abstaining.

On Uposatha days, monastics recite the Patimokkha (code of discipline). Devout laity observe Eight Precepts, including no solid food after noon. Emphasis on meditation and restraint, not ritualistic fasting.
Most sacred Buddhist day celebrating Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and parinirvana. Vegetarian food, meditation, charity. Some observe no food after midday.
Harvest festival. Some families fast the day before. Khichdi, til-gur (sesame-jaggery) laddoo, and pongal (sweet rice) are traditional foods. Not primarily a fasting festival but diet is special.
NOT a fasting tradition — included because the elaborate vegetarian feast (Onam Sadhya with 26+ dishes on banana leaf) is an important dietary planning event for Thali app.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Sabudana (sago/tapioca pearls), potato, sweet potato, raw banana, peanuts, coconut, sendha namak (rock salt), rajgira/amaranth flour, singhara/water chestnut flour, kuttu/buckwheat flour, all fruits, milk, curd, paneer, ghee, sugar, dry fruits (cashew, almond, raisin), sama ke chawal (barnyard millet — looks like rice but is not a grain), makhana (fox nuts)
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: ALL grains (rice, wheat, barley, jowar, bajra, ragi, maize), ALL pulses/lentils (toor, moong, chana, urad, masoor, rajma), regular iodised salt, onion, garlic, turmeric (some traditions), mustard seeds (some traditions), fenugreek, asafoetida/hing (some traditions), non-veg, eggs
foodRules.specialSaltRule: Only sendha namak (rock salt) — regular salt forbidden
foodRules.cookingOilAllowed: Ghee and peanut oil — mustard oil debated
foodRules.dairyAllowed: YES — all dairy allowed (milk, curd, paneer, ghee, butter)
foodRules.grainsAllowed: NO grains or pulses. Pseudo-cereals allowed: rajgira, kuttu, singhara, sama ke chawal
foodRules.timeRestriction: One meal a day (some traditions); parana next morning after Hari Vasara ends
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: KEY LOGIC: Check ingredient list for ANY grain/pulse — if found, recipe is NOT Ekadashi-safe. Replace regular salt with sendha namak in all recipes.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Kuttu (buckwheat) flour, singhara (water chestnut) flour, sabudana, potato, sweet potato, pumpkin/kaddu, lauki/bottle gourd, arbi/colocasia, all dairy (milk, curd, paneer, ghee, makhan), fruits, dry fruits, makhana, coconut, sendha namak, green chillies, black pepper, cumin/jeera, coriander leaves, ginger (allowed in most traditions), sugar, jaggery
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: ALL grains (rice, wheat, millet etc.), ALL lentils/dal, onion, garlic, regular salt, non-veg, eggs, alcohol, tobacco, mushrooms, turnip, brinjal/eggplant (in some traditions)
foodRules.cookingOilAllowed: Ghee, peanut oil, or coconut oil
foodRules.dairyAllowed: YES — all dairy allowed and encouraged
foodRules.grainsAllowed: NO regular grains. Kuttu, singhara, rajgira flour are allowed (technically pseudo-cereals)
foodRules.timeRestriction: Usually 2 meals or 1 meal per day; varies by family strictness
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: KEY LOGIC: Very similar to Ekadashi rules but slightly more relaxed. Ginger is usually allowed (unlike some Ekadashi traditions). 9-day duration means meal variety is important — don't repeat the same dish.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Fruits, milk, curd, one vegetarian meal (varies by family), some allow all veg food
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Non-veg, eggs, alcohol. Some strict observers avoid salt and grains.
foodRules.specialSaltRule: Regular salt usually OK unless observer is very strict
foodRules.grainsAllowed: Varies — strict observers avoid grains; moderate ones eat one veg meal
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Most flexible Hindu weekly fast. Default to: one vegetarian meal in evening. Ask user for strictness level.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Red-colored foods preferred (jaggery, pomegranate). One meal: wheat roti, lentils, jaggery. Some do fruit-only.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Non-veg, eggs, alcohol. Some avoid salt and wheat.
foodRules.specialSaltRule: Varies by tradition — usually regular salt OK
foodRules.grainsAllowed: Usually allowed except in very strict forms
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Least standardized weekly fast. Default to one veg meal. Red/orange foods are thematic.

foodRules.allowedFoods: YELLOW foods specifically: chana dal, besan (chickpea flour), banana, turmeric (haldi), kesar (saffron), yellow rice, yellow cloth is worn. One meal a day with yellow lentils.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Non-veg, eggs, alcohol. Some avoid salt. No washing hair (superstition, not dietary).
foodRules.grainsAllowed: Yes — yellow rice or chana dal dishes encouraged
foodRules.timeRestriction: One meal a day, should be before sunset
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Thematic color = yellow. Suggest chana dal, besan dishes, banana desserts. Fun to implement visually.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Sweet foods, milk products, white foods. Kheer, halwa, fruits, sugar. One meal.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: SOUR foods specifically forbidden: lemon, tamarind, imli, citrus fruits, pickles/achaar, vinegar, curd (some traditions). No non-veg, no salt (some traditions).
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Key differentiator is NO SOUR foods. Check recipes for tamarind, lemon, amchur, curd, tomato (debated).

foodRules.allowedFoods: BLACK foods: urad dal, black sesame (til), mustard oil, black grapes, black salt, kale. One meal.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Non-veg, eggs, alcohol, mustard (in some traditions). Some avoid salt.
foodRules.timeRestriction: Some eat only after sunset; others one meal at any time
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Thematic color = black. Suggest urad dal dishes, til ladoo. Saturday evening meal tradition.

foodRules.allowedFoods: NOTHING during the fast (nirjala — no food, no water). Sargi (pre-dawn meal prepared by MIL): mathri, dry fruits, feni, sweets, fruits, parathas. Post-moonrise: water first, then feast.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Everything during fast hours (sunrise to moonrise)
foodRules.timeRestriction: Nirjala (no water, no food) from sunrise until moon sighting at night. Sargi eaten before dawn.
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Binary fast — nothing during, feast after. Plan only the Sargi (pre-dawn) and post-moonrise dinner. The dinner is typically elaborate — suggest festive North Indian meal.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Thekua (wheat flour + jaggery sweet), fruits (especially sugarcane, banana, coconut), rice, ghee. Prasad items only. Strictly vegetarian. No onion/garlic throughout.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Onion, garlic, non-veg, eggs, anything containing preservatives or artificial colors. No tasting food while cooking (cook must not taste).
foodRules.specialSaltRule: Regular salt OK in prasad preparation
foodRules.timeRestriction: Main fast: 36 hours nirjala. Day before: eat one kharna meal (rice kheer + roti). Day after: break fast after sunrise arghya.
foodRules.waterAllowed: NO — 36 hours nirjala during main fast
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Plan the Kharna meal (day before) and the feast (day after). The 36-hour fast day itself has NO food/water.

foodRules.allowedFoods: All above-ground vegetables, all grains, all pulses/lentils, dairy (milk, ghee, curd, paneer), fruits, dry fruits, sugar, spices (except those listed as forbidden), cooking oils
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: ALL root vegetables permanently: potato, onion, garlic, ginger, carrot, radish, beetroot, turnip, sweet potato, yam, shalgam. Also: non-veg, eggs, honey, mushrooms (grow on decaying matter), eggplant/brinjal (has many seeds = many lives). NO eating after sunset.
foodRules.dairyAllowed: YES — dairy is central to Jain diet
foodRules.grainsAllowed: YES — all grains and pulses allowed
foodRules.timeRestriction: MUST finish eating before sunset — no food after dark (to avoid harming insects attracted to light/food)
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: CRITICAL LOGIC: This is ALWAYS active for Jain users. Every recipe must be checked: no potato, no onion, no garlic, no ginger, no root vegs. This is the most impactful dietary filter in the app.

foodRules.allowedFoods: During Ayambil: ONE meal of PLAIN boiled grains/pulses only — no oil, no ghee, no spices, no salt, no sugar, no milk. During Ekasana: one normal Jain meal. During Upvas: only boiled water.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Everything beyond what's specified for the chosen fast type. Root vegetables are already permanently forbidden. Additional: green leafy vegetables, fermented foods.
foodRules.grainsAllowed: Yes — plain boiled only during Ayambil
foodRules.timeRestriction: All food before sunset. During Upvas: no food at all, only boiled water before sunset.
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Paryushana has MULTIPLE fasting intensities. Ask user which level: Ayambil (strictest food), Ekasana (one meal), Upvas (no food), or Atthai (8 days no food). Generate accordingly.

foodRules.allowedFoods: ONE meal per day: only boiled grains and pulses. No oil, spices, salt, sugar, ghee, milk, dry fruits. Just plain boiled food.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Oil, ghee, butter, spices of any kind, salt, sugar, jaggery, milk, curd, all root vegetables, green leafy vegetables
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: This is Ayambil rules for 9 days. Very restrictive. Suggest variety through different grain/pulse combinations each day: Day 1 = rice, Day 2 = wheat, Day 3 = moong dal, etc.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Suhoor (pre-dawn): High-energy, slow-digesting foods — dates, eggs, oatmeal/porridge, banana, whole wheat roti, curd/lassi, nuts, chicken. Iftar (sunset): Dates + water first (Sunnah), then: fruit chaat, samosa, pakora, shorba/soup, biryani, kebabs, haleem, phirni, sheer khurma. ALL halal food is allowed.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: All non-halal food (pork, alcohol permanently; non-halal meat). During fasting hours: ALL food, water, smoking, chewing gum are forbidden.
foodRules.timeRestriction: No food/water from Fajr (pre-dawn, ~4:30-5:00 AM) to Maghrib (sunset, ~6:30-7:00 PM). Times vary by location and date.
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Two meals only — Suhoor and Iftar. Suhoor should be HIGH ENERGY + SLOW DIGESTING (complex carbs, protein, fiber). Iftar should start light (dates + water) then build. Calculate fasting hours based on user's city coordinates.

foodRules.allowedFoods: All halal food. No special restrictions beyond normal halal rules.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: Non-halal food (pork, alcohol, non-halal meat). During fasting hours: all food and water.
foodRules.timeRestriction: Dawn to sunset (same as Ramadan format). 1-2 days only.
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Same fasting format as Ramadan but only 1-2 days. Plan normal halal suhoor and iftar.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Langar: Simple, nutritious vegetarian food. Typical: roti, dal, sabzi, rice, kheer. NO distinction by caste/class — everyone eats together on the floor.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: No halal/jhatka distinction in langar (use jhatka if non-veg, but most langars are vegetarian). No alcohol, no tobacco.
foodRules.timeRestriction: No fasting tradition — Langar is about COMMUNAL EATING not abstaining
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Sikhism is ANTI-fasting. For Sikh users, don't suggest fasting. Instead, suggest langar-style simple meals on Gurpurabs. Respect this philosophical difference.

foodRules.allowedFoods: Vegetarian food only before noon. After noon: only liquids (water, juice, tea without milk in some traditions). Fruits sometimes allowed in afternoon in Mahayana.
foodRules.forbiddenFoods: All non-veg, eggs (on Uposatha days). Solid food after noon.
foodRules.dairyAllowed: Varies by tradition — Theravada may avoid dairy
foodRules.timeRestriction: No solid food after noon (12 PM). Morning meal should be complete and sufficient.
foodRules.notesForAppLogic: LOGIC: Plan a substantial vegetarian breakfast/brunch. No lunch or dinner. This is a minority practice in India — include for completeness.

substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Provides similar bulk and mild sweetness when cooked. Add hing for flavor.
Does not replace texture but adds the savory/umami depth. Use along with raw banana for best result.

substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 medium onion = ½ cup grated lauki
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Melts into gravies like onion does. Mild flavor.
Hing provides a similar pungent, savory flavor. Note: some strict Ekadashi observers avoid hing too.
Saunth is allowed in most Jain traditions (it's dried, not fresh root). Check with user. Provides warmth and flavor.
Very similar texture when cooked. Works in sabzi, cutlets, tikkis.

substitutions.substitutionType: Direct substitute — BUT check if user considers yam a root veg
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Some Jain families consider suran acceptable; others don't. ASK the user.
Much lower GI. Works in aloo gobi, paratha filling. Mash for similar texture.

substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 cup rice = 1 cup sama ke chawal
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Looks and cooks like rice. Allowed on Ekadashi as it's technically a grass seed, not a grain.

substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 cup white rice = 1 cup brown rice OR 1.5 cups cauliflower rice
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Brown rice: lower GI, more fiber, takes longer to cook. Cauliflower rice: very low carb but different texture.
Kuttu roti is dense and earthy. Cooks differently — needs less water, breaks easily. Add boiled potato for binding.
Light and starchy. Great for puris and halwa. Not good for roti (too sticky).

substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 cup atta = ¾ cup rajgira flour
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Very nutritious. Mix with boiled potato for binding. Makes thin, crisp rotis.
Slightly milder and mineral-y taste. Chemically: NaCl without iodine additives. Available at all grocery stores during festivals.
Press tofu well, marinate before cooking. Less fat, more protein. Texture is softer.
Adds richness to curries. Slightly sweet. Works well in South Indian and Bengali cooking.
Available in metro cities. Can be made at home with coconut milk + vegan culture.
No calories, no glycemic impact. Taste is slightly different. Works in kheer, halwa. NOT suitable for caramelizing.

substitutions.substituteIngredient: Olive oil / Rice bran oil (limited qty)
substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 tbsp ghee = 1 tbsp oil (but less flavor)
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Loses the distinctive ghee aroma. For tadka, use minimal oil + hing for flavor.
During Ayambil, food is deliberately bland. The point is austerity. Do not try to replicate flavor.
Some strict Ekadashi observers avoid turmeric. Most families DO use it. Ask user preference.

substitutions.quantityAdjustment: ½ tsp mustard = ½ tsp cumin
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Cumin is universally allowed across almost all Hindu fasts. Safe default for tadka.

substitutions.substituteIngredient: Curd (for tang) or raw mango powder (amchur)
substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 medium tomato → 2 tbsp curd or ½ tsp amchur
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Most families DO use tomato during Navratri. Some strict ones avoid it. Ask user.

substitutions.quantityAdjustment: 1 egg = 3 tbsp besan slurry OR 1 mashed banana (in baking)
substitutions.flavorTextureNotes: Besan works for coating/binding in cooking. Banana works for moisture in baking.
Jaggery is universally accepted across Jain traditions. Provides similar sweetness with mineral richness.

appLogicRules.action: THEN remove ALL recipes containing: potato, onion, garlic, ginger, carrot, radish, beetroot, turnip, sweet potato from their meal options. This is ALWAYS active, not just on fasting days.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If a recipe is Jain-safe but contains ginger, suggest it with ginger replaced by saunth (dry ginger powder)
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Family has 1 Jain member + 4 non-Jain. The Jain member gets a separate sabzi without onion/potato while others get regular aloo gobi.

appLogicRules.condition: IF today == Ekadashi AND member.observes_ekadashi == True
appLogicRules.action: THEN remove ALL grain-based recipes (rice, roti, dal) and replace with: sabudana khichdi, kuttu roti, singhara puri, fruit, milk dishes. Replace regular salt with sendha namak.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If member also observes Monday fast AND today is Monday Ekadashi, apply Ekadashi rules (stricter)
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Dadi observes Ekadashi. She gets sabudana khichdi while family gets regular dal-chawal. Kitchen cooks both.

appLogicRules.action: THEN either: (a) reduce portion size to bring carbs within limit, OR (b) substitute high-GI ingredient with low-GI alternative (white rice → brown rice, potato → cauliflower)
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If Ekadashi forces sabudana (high carb) for a diabetic, suggest fruit + curd instead (both Ekadashi-safe and low-GI)
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Dadaji is diabetic with 45g carb limit. Family is having rajma-chawal. Dadaji gets rajma with brown rice, smaller portion, extra salad.

appLogicRules.action: THEN replace paneer → tofu, milk → coconut milk, curd → coconut curd, ghee → oil in that member's portion. Flag recipes that have dairy as a base ingredient (shahi paneer, kheer, raita).
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If Navratri menu relies heavily on dairy (curd, paneer, milk), suggest coconut-based alternatives for this member
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Mother is lactose intolerant. Family's Navratri menu has sabudana khichdi with curd. Mother gets hers with coconut curd instead.

appLogicRules.condition: IF today is within Navratri_dates AND member.observes_navratri == True
appLogicRules.action: THEN apply Navratri food rules for 9 days. Use only kuttu/singhara/rajgira flour. No grains, no onion/garlic. Sendha namak. Suggest variety across 9 days to avoid repetition.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If member is BOTH Jain AND observing Navratri, Jain rules are stricter — apply Jain rules as base, then add Navratri restrictions on top
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Dadi observes Navratri, family doesn't. For 9 days, Dadi gets separate Navratri thali while family eats normally. Plan so Dadi doesn't eat the same sabudana khichdi all 9 days.

appLogicRules.condition: IF member.religion == "Muslim" AND today is within Ramadan_dates
appLogicRules.action: THEN restructure meal plan: NO lunch/snacks. Only Suhoor (high-energy pre-dawn meal) and Iftar (sunset meal). Calculate local sunrise/sunset times for the member's city.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If Muslim member is fasting Ramadan while Hindu member is observing Navratri at the same time, plan BOTH accommodations from the same kitchen
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: March 2026: Ramadan and Chaitra Navratri overlap for some days. Muslim mother fasting Ramadan, Hindu grandmother fasting Navratri. Kitchen must produce: Suhoor (4:30 AM), Navratri thali (lunch), Iftar (6:30 PM), and regular dinner.

appLogicRules.action: THEN remove: whole nuts (choking hazard), honey (botulism risk for under-1), very spicy dishes, raw salad, hard/crunchy items. Make all food soft-textured. No artificial sweeteners.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: Toddler version of any dish = same dish but mashed/softened, less spice, no whole nuts
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Family has dal makhani with butter naan. Toddler gets the same dal but thinned and mashed, with soft roti torn into pieces. No whole cashews from the garnish.

appLogicRules.action: THEN prefer: khichdi, soft dal, dalia, idli, curd rice, soup, soft sabzi. Avoid: hard roti, raw vegetables, tough meat, dry snacks, very fibrous foods.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: Can combine with diabetic rules — soft + low-GI is possible (moong dal khichdi is both)
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Dadaji (75) and Dadi (72) both need softer food. Moong dal khichdi with ghee works for both and is also easy to make diabetic-friendly.

appLogicRules.condition: IF today == Friday AND member.observes_friday_fast == True
appLogicRules.action: THEN remove recipes containing: lemon, tamarind, amchur (dry mango), imli, citrus, vinegar, pickles. Curd is debated — ask user preference.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: If Friday coincides with Ekadashi, apply Ekadashi rules (stricter)
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Mother observes Friday fast for Santoshi Maa. No dal with lemon, no tomato-based curries (tomato is sour), no raita with imli.

appLogicRules.action: THEN prefer: seasonal vegetables (cheaper), dal over paneer, egg over chicken, local grains. Avoid: dry fruits, exotic fruits, paneer-heavy dishes, out-of-season vegetables.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: Budget + fasting can be expensive (kuttu flour costs 3x wheat). Flag this to user: "Navratri meals will be ₹120/day more than usual due to special ingredients"
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Budget is ₹300/day. Instead of paneer tikka, suggest egg curry (₹40 vs ₹150). Instead of dry fruit garnish, suggest roasted peanuts.

appLogicRules.condition: IF two or more recipes in the week use the same base ingredient
appLogicRules.action: THEN batch-schedule them on consecutive days. E.g., if Monday and Wednesday both need chana dal, buy once and use twice.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: Don't let this override dietary/fasting rules — convenience yields to correctness
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Monday: Chana dal + roti. Tuesday: Dal fry with leftover chana dal + jeera rice. Same dal, two different meals.

appLogicRules.condition: IF today is within Paryushana AND member.is_jain == True
appLogicRules.action: THEN ask fasting level: (a) Ayambil = one plain boiled meal, no oil/spice/salt/dairy, (b) Ekasana = one normal Jain meal, (c) Upvas = no food, only boiled water, (d) Atthai = 8 days no food. Apply the selected level.
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: Different Jain family members may choose different levels. Dadi may do Atthai while teenager does Ekasana. Plan separately.
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: During Paryushana: Jain Dadi does Ayambil (plain rice with water), Jain father does Ekasana (one dal-roti-sabzi meal), non-Jain mother eats normally. Three different plans from one kitchen.

appLogicRules.action: THEN prefer vegetables in season for that month. Flag out-of-season vegetables as "expensive/low quality right now".
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: Fasting ingredients override seasonal — sabudana is needed for Ekadashi regardless of season
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: August: suggest lauki, tori, bhindi, karela (monsoon vegetables). Avoid: matar, sarson ka saag (winter vegetables — expensive and bad quality in August).

appLogicRules.condition: IF member.is_jain == True AND member.strict_timing == True
appLogicRules.action: THEN all meals must be completed before sunset. Calculate local sunset time. Dinner must be planned early (5:00-6:30 PM depending on season).
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: During winter when sunset is 5:30 PM, dinner at 5:00 PM may conflict with work schedules. Flag this to user.
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Strict Jain member must finish dinner by 6:15 PM (August sunset). Plan an early dinner that's complete and nutritious.

appLogicRules.condition: IF member has TWO fasting traditions active on the same day
appLogicRules.action: THEN apply the STRICTER of the two. E.g., if Ekadashi falls on a Monday (Somvar Vrat), Ekadashi rules are stricter → apply Ekadashi. If Jain daily rules + Paryushana, apply Paryushana (stricter).
appLogicRules.conflictResolution: When in doubt, the rule that restricts MORE foods takes priority. Union of forbidden foods, intersection of allowed foods.
appLogicRules.exampleScenario: Monday Ekadashi: Dadi observes both Somvar Vrat and Ekadashi. Ekadashi forbids grains; Monday fast only restricts to one meal. Apply Ekadashi rules + one meal limit = sabudana khichdi as the single meal.
